object_context: Geometric/deformation root child H4d1. For a smooth projective family f:X->S, a point s0, and a locally flat rational class alpha that is algebraic on X_s0, let T be an irreducible Hodge-locus branch on which alpha remains type (p,p). Identify the weakest checkable condition under which a class-constrained algebraic-cycle realization space has a component dominating T. Keep separate Hodge persistence, existence of some algebraic realization, deformation of a chosen witness, rational linear combinations, formal lifting, algebraization, monodromy, and global continuation.
structural_coordinates: root coefficients are rational; integral Hodge counterexamples are outside the exact root target
fibers are smooth projective complex algebraic varieties
alpha is a flat/parallel-transported cohomology class and T is defined by persistence of Hodge type
Cattani-Deligne-Kaplan controls algebraicity of the Hodge locus but does not construct a representing cycle
algebraic-cycle realization is a witness-lifting problem from a cohomological compatibility locus
a rational cycle may require a signed rational linear combination, not one effective point of a Hilbert scheme
local deformation of a chosen cycle can be obstructed even when the cohomology class remains Hodge unless extra hypotheses such as semiregularity control the obstruction
formal pro-class lifting and actual algebraic/global cycle lifting are distinct steps
singularities of relative cycle spaces, monodromy, and singular/compactified boundary fibers can obstruct globalization
the atom assumes one algebraic starting witness and therefore cannot by itself solve the root initial-existence gap for an arbitrary Hodge class
equivalent_formulations: dominance of a suitable class-constrained relative Chow/cycle realization space over the Hodge-locus branch T
local lifting of a Hodge-compatible base deformation to an algebraic-cycle deformation with fixed cohomology class
comparison between the tangent/obstruction theory of the cycle realization space and the tangent equations defining the Hodge locus
formal lifting along infinitesimal thickenings followed by an explicit algebraization and continuation obligation
identify when the image of cycle realizations with class alpha contains a neighborhood or irreducible component of T
solved_analogues: codimension-one divisor classes: Lefschetz (1,1) plus Picard/line-bundle geometry realizes integral (1,1) classes
semiregular relative deformation settings where obstruction theory matches Hodge persistence under the theorem's hypotheses
near_solved_analogues: Cattani-Deligne-Kaplan algebraicity of the Hodge locus for a fixed class in a variation of Hodge structure
Bloch-Esnault-Kerz formal deformation of rational algebraic cycle classes under additional Chow-Kunneth-type structure, including abelian-scheme applications
explicit variational-Hodge results for special cycle configurations such as semiregular subvarieties or selected hypersurface cycles

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A compatibility condition defines a feasible locus in observable/base space, while actual solutions live in a separate witness space mapping to that base. Knowing the base point satisfies the compatibility equations is weaker than proving a witness exists or that the witness projection is locally onto.
common_abstraction: base compatibility locus versus witness realization space
projection from witnesses to admissible base states
local surjectivity requires tangent control plus obstruction control, not only equations on the base
source_to_target_mapping: observable compatibility locus -> Hodge locus T
witness space -> relative algebraic-cycle realization space
witness projection -> map from cycle realizations to S
linearized compatibility -> infinitesimal variation of Hodge structure
shared_constraints: base compatibility is necessary but may not be sufficient for witness existence
local tangent surjectivity can fail because of higher-order obstructions
global continuation may fail even after local lifting
disanalogies: algebraic cycles have rational equivalence and coefficient issues absent from a generic smooth inverse problem
the witness space may be singular, reducible, non-fine, or require Chow rather than Hilbert/Kuranishi parameterization
monodromy and algebraization are arithmetic/algebro-geometric constraints not modeled by a generic implicit-function theorem
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Treat Hodge persistence only as the base compatibility equation; search for a separately verifiable witness-projection criterion with tangent, obstruction, coefficient, algebraization, and monodromy obligations.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Before retaining any concrete lifting criterion, verify it on the divisor/Picard case and a semiregular case, then test a non-semiregular or formally-liftable-but-not-yet-global setting to show the criterion distinguishes the missing obstruction instead of restating Hodge persistence.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Structural proposal analogy only; it supplies no Hodge-theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned divisor/Picard geometry, Hodge-locus algebraicity, semiregularity, formal deformation, normal-function perspectives, and generic inverse/constraint-lifting structure. Retained only the witness-projection analogy because it cleanly separates necessary base equations from geometric realization and comes with exact target-domain calibration obligations.
